To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the pedagogical principle of representation and exaggeration in the context of 3 vs.3 small-sided games did not have an effect on game performance of U-10 soccer players.

both games could offer similar degeneracy to the players for their skill acquisition (specific contextualized task constraints that allow the players to develop their game performance capabilities and the ability to achieve different outcomes depending on the context).
the use of the pedagogical principles representation and exaggeration in Game-based approaches did not lead to differences in decision-making and execution abilities in youth soccer players.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of small-sided games in the development of game performance in young soccer players.
the pedagogical principles used in Game-based approaches and the way that we should use smallsized games in Game-based approach.
the use of two task constraints (representation and exaggeration) and their effects on decision-making and execution in small-sided games in youth soccer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both games were effective in the acquisition of soccer-specific skills.

both games were effective in developing players' capabilities for adapting their behaviors to changing performance situations, and that the pedagogical principles used in this study were effective for developing players' game performance.
both games were equally effective for skill acquisition in youth soccer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have to use small-sided games with different task constraints in Game-based approaches to promote skill acquisition and game performance in youth soccer.
the use of representation or exaggeration of the task constraints of small-sided games is not necessary to provide similar degeneracies for players in order to develop their game performance.
both games had a positive effect on the development of the players’ game performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can use both pedagogical principles (representation and exaggeration) in small-sided games, but it is important to be aware of the task constraints of the game to be able to use them in a more effective and efficient way.
we should not focus only on the number of constraints, but on the nature of the constraints, to understand how the game is being played and how the player is learning.
both games can be used to develop players’ capabilities to achieve different outcomes, and to provide the degeneracy processes for skill acquisition.
